reconstructed_theorem_text: For all real a,b,C,epsilon with a<=b, C>=0 and epsilon>0, and every measurable f:R->R satisfying 0<=f(t)<=C for Lebesgue-almost every t in [a,b], there exists a globally C-infinity function g:R->R such that 0<g(t)<=C+epsilon for every t in [a,b], and the Lebesgue set integral over [a,b] of |g(t)-f(t)| is strictly less than epsilon.
objects: Real endpoints a,b; real bound C; real tolerance epsilon.
Globally measurable real function f and existential globally smooth real function g.
Lebesgue measure restricted to the closed interval [a,b].
domains: Bounds and errors concern Icc a b=[a,b], while smoothness of g is on all R.
quantifiers: For every a,b,C,epsilon and f satisfying the hypotheses, there exists one g satisfying all conclusions.
The bound on f is almost everywhere for volume.restrict(Icc a b).
The strict lower bound and upper bound on g hold pointwise for every t in [a,b], including both endpoints.
assumptions: f is measurable on all R.
f belongs to [0,C] almost everywhere on [a,b]; no everywhere bound is assumed.
conclusion: ContDiff R (up-arrow top) g: g is C-infinity on R.
For every t in [a,b], 0<g(t) and g(t)<=C+epsilon.
Integral_[a,b] |g-f| dt < epsilon, a strict L1-error estimate.
scopes: One and the same g satisfies smoothness, positivity, boundedness and the error bound.
No bound on g outside [a,b] is asserted.
No uniform positive lower constant, uniform pointwise approximation to f, or sequence of approximants is asserted.
constant_dependencies: The witness g may depend on a,b,C,epsilon and f.
The displayed upper bound is C+epsilon, and the integral tolerance is exactly epsilon; no interval-length normalization occurs.

semantic_checks.totalized_integrals: The syntax is a totalized Bochner set integral. Here f is integrable on the finite interval by its AE bound, and smooth g is bounded and integrable there; thus |g-f| is integrable and the error inequality has genuine L1 meaning.
semantic_checks.ae_pointwise_order: AE f-range does not become a pointwise range. The conclusion on g is pointwise everywhere on the closed interval.
semantic_checks.pushforwards: No pushforward measure or hidden law.
semantic_checks.interval_orientation: This is a set integral for volume.restrict(Icc a b), not oriented intervalIntegral notation. The explicit a<=b hypothesis fixes the order.
semantic_checks.exponents: The error is the first power |g-f|, with no square or root.
semantic_checks.compactness: No abstract compact state space; the real closed bounded interval is compact.
semantic_checks.zero_endpoints: a=b and C=0 are both allowed. For a=b the error integral is zero but g must still be strictly positive and <=C+epsilon at that point.
semantic_checks.absolute_continuity: Global C-infinity regularity is asserted for g; no absolute-continuity assumption on f.
semantic_checks.derivative_domain: No particular derivative identity; all smoothness is global on R.
